title: Sohila and sleep
tomorrow: how do prayer, gurdwara and seva all fit into one week?

cards: Before a Punjabi wedding, there's a moment when the date is set and the family gathers to pour oil and give blessings. The Sikh bedtime prayer, Kirtan Sohila, opens its first hymn on that picture.
In paraphrase: the wedding day is written; come, friends, pour the oil, and bless me that I may meet my Lord. A wedding, at bedtime. The meeting it means is the soul's, with the One.

teach.h: SOHILA: SHORT, BUILT FOR THE DARK.
teach.b: Sohila is short, a handful of hymns, and it's built for the dark.

teach.h: A HOUSE WHERE PRAISE IS SUNG.
teach.b: The first hymn asks for a house where the Creator's praises are sung and reflected on, and in that house, it says, sing the song of praise.
Then, later, comes Guru Nanak's Arti, and it's made of things you can see from a window.

In paraphrase: the sky is the plate, the sun and moon are the lamps, the stars are the pearls on it. The scented breeze from the hills is the incense, the wind is the fan, and all the forests are flowers.
What a worship this is, the hymn says, and it's being done for you, all night, by the world itself. So Sohila doesn't ask you to light anything.

It points out that the lamps are already lit. Sikhs say it at night before sleep, and it's also sung at the end of a life, which gives the wedding picture its full weight. Rest, in that light, isn't the day stopping.

how: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila at night before sleeping; it is also recited at the close of the day in the gurdwara, when the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest, and at the end of a funeral.

o: the night hymns said before rest, the sky as the lamp-plate
a prayer asking for protection from bad dreams
a lullaby sung to children before they fall asleep

games.q: the night sky in Sohila — tap the pairs.

s: Kirtan Sohila is said only at funerals

Guru Nanak's Arti makes the sky the plate and the sun and moon the lamps
the stars are the pearls, the forests the flowers.
Sohila's first hymn uses a wedding picture

games.q: a friend sleeping over hears you read Sohila and asks why a bedtime prayer sounds like a wedding. what's the best answer?
o: it pictures the soul's meeting with the One as a wedding day, said each night.
it was first written for a Sikh wedding and kept the song's words by habit.
Sikh weddings take place at night, so the bedtime prayer borrows the picture.
games.why: the first hymn of Sohila uses the wedding as a picture of meeting the Lord, which is why it's sung at night and at life's end.

practice: Turn the lights down, or go to a window. Find whatever light is left, a streetlamp, the moon, a phone's glow on the ceiling, and name it as the hymn would: a lamp on the plate.
Then close your eyes and let the sit be dark and quiet.

wordCard.voice: Sohila and sleep. The night hymns, Kirtan Sohila, said before rest: the sky as the plate, sun and moon as lamps.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sohila, a song of praise: the night prayer.

carryVoice: Keep this: sleep in praise, with the lamps lit tonight without any help from you. Rest well.
